Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11046
AUTHORIZING AWARD OF THE BRONZE STAR MEDAL
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States and as Commander in Chief of the armed forces of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1. The Bronze Star Medal, with accompanying ribbons and ap­
purtenances, which was first established by Executive Order No. 9419 
of February 4, 1944, may be awarded by the Secretary of a military 
department or the Secretary of the Treasury with regard to the 
Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, or by such 
military commanders, or other appropriate officers as the Secretary 
concerned may designate, to any person who, while serving in any 
capacity in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or 
Coast Guard of the United States, after December 6, 1941, dis­
tinguishes, or has distinguished, himself by heroic or meritorious 
achievement or service, not involving participation in aerial flight—
(a) while engaged in an action against an enemy of the United 
States;
(b) while engaged in military operations involving conflict with 
an opposing foreign force; or
(c) while serving with friendly foreign forces engaged in an armed 
conflict against an opposing armed force in which the United States 
is not a belligerent party.
2. The Bronze Star Medal and appurtenances thereto shall be of 
appropriate design approved by the Secretary of Defense, and shall 
be awarded under such regulations as the Secretary concerned may 
prescribe. Such regulations shall, so far as practicable, be uniform, 
and those of the military departments shall be subject to the approval 
of the Secretary of Defense.
3. No more than one Bronze Star Medal shall be awarded to any 
one person, but for each succeeding heroic or meritorious achieveiiient 
or service justifying such an award a suitable device may be awarded 
to be worn with the medal as prescribed by appropriate regulations.
4. The Bronze Star Medal or device may be awarded posthumously 
and, when so awarded, may be presented to such representative of 
the deceased as may be deemed appropriate by the Secretary of the 
department concerned.
5. This order shall supersede Executive Order No. 9419 of February 
4, 1944, entitled “Bronze Star Medal”. However, existing regula­
tions prescribed under that order shall, so far as they are not incon­
sistent with this order, remain in effect until modified or revoked by 
regulations prescribed under this order by the Secretary of the 
department concerned.
J o h n F . K ennedy
T h e W h it e H ouse ,
August 24, 1962.
[F.R. Doc. 62-8714; Filed, Aug. 27, 1962; 11:25 a.m.]

research_rationale:
EO 11046 (27 FR 8575, signed 1962-08-24; held official Federal Register text, page location high) authorizes the Secretaries of the military departments (and the Coast Guard's Secretary) to award the Bronze Star Medal (paragraph 1 with subparagraphs (a)-(c)), sets design and regulations (2), limits to one medal with devices (3), allows posthumous award (4), and supersedes EO 9419 while keeping existing regulations until replaced (5). It rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief, not on a statute, so no authority statute can have lapsed. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition subsequent or revocation. Later instruments found by name or by number in the held texts: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation in paragraph 1), EO 13286 section 70 (68 FR 10619; effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security in section 1) and EO 14085 section 4 (87 FR 60541, signed 2022-10-03; paragraph 1 wording, Space Force). All three amend paragraph 1 only and none revokes or supersedes the order. The Code (release point 119-121) prints the order in full as a note to 10 U.S.C. 7276, as amended by those three orders, with no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are exactly these three amendments. research_rationale:
EO 11079 (28 FR 819, signed 1963-01-25; held official Federal Register text, page location high) is a single designation made under section 2603 of title 10, United States Code: the Secretary of Defense (Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps members), the Secretary of the Treasury (Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy) and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (commissioned officers of the Public Health Service) are to prescribe regulations under which members may accept fellowships, scholarships or grants, uniform so far as practicable. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition or revocation. Three later orders changed the officers named: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation), EO 12608 section 15 (1987-09-09; Health, Education, and Welfare to Health and Human Services) and EO 13286 section 69 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security). None revokes or supersedes the order. The Code prints the order as amended by all three as a note to 10 U.S.C. 2603, so the authority section named in the order is still in the Code, and the note carries no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are the three amendments. research_rationale:
EO 11231 (30 FR 8665, signed 1965-07-08; held official Federal Register text, page location high) establishes the Vietnam Service Medal (section 1), lets members who qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal by Vietnam service between July 1, 1958 and July 4, 1965 remain qualified for it or exchange it on application for the Vietnam Service Medal (section 2) and allows posthumous award (section 3). It rests on the President's authority as President and Commander in Chief, not on a statute. No Code note prints this order, so no CURRENT record is held; the current predicate therefore rests on the route original plus bounded searches: the held original, every held later instrument attached as an event, no own-terms end, and the three bounded machine searches read for their stated coverage. Later instruments: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation in section 1) and EO 13286 section 66 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security in section 1). Neither revokes or supersedes the order, and the ofr_catalog disposition record held in jobs/peano-formulario lists exactly these two amendments and no revocation. Own-terms signal: section 1 awards the medal for service 'before a terminal date to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense'. That is a limit on which service qualifies, set under the order itself; the same held OFR record notes that the terminal date was set as March 28, 1973 by the Secretary of Defense (DoD Instruction 1348.15 memo of January 26, 1973) and that service after it did not qualify. It does not end the command to award the medal for qualifying service or the exchange right in section 2: the held current Army regulation AR 600-8-22 (a source-ladder capture of the edition that supersedes the 30 July 2025 edition) says in its paragraph 2-13 that the Vietnam Service Medal 'was established by EO 11231, 8 July 1965, as amended by EO 13286', is awarded for service in Vietnam after 3 July 1965 through 28 March 1973, and that on request a person qualified for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal may be awarded the Vietnam Service Medal instead. That regulation is held in the repository but is not one of the packet's citable evidence records, so it is described here and not used as a claim source. Cutoff limit: the bounded Code and eCFR searches were run for the cutoff but this order has no hit in the Code notes; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected in the held Code edition (current through 2026-10-09).
